input.final_summary: Found four Important correctness/deployment issues: policy rows are never created or synchronized by normal asset editing, posted-period locking fails open on database errors, the migration patch rolls back by default, and historical office/place display reads mutable master data instead of ledger snapshots. No Critical issue was identified.

content.text:
No Critical findings. Four Important findings remain.

1. Important — New and edited assets never create or synchronize a depreciation policy  
   Files:
   - `1.WIN-FORM/FamManager/Device/frmDeviceDetail.cs:530-578`
   - `1.WIN-FORM/FamObject/FAM_DeviceDepPolicy.cs:5-17`
   - `2.SQL/patches/2026-10-19/FAM-DeviceDep/02_20261019_FAM_DeviceDepPolicy_migrate.sql:145-181`

   `SaveData()` writes `IsLineDep`, start date and useful life only to `FAM_Device`. The new policy class exposes only lookup/lock checks, and the only policy insert in patches is the one-time migration. Consequently:
   - assets created after deployment never enter Preview/Post;
   - pre-post changes to `UsingDate`, `UsingLengthMonth`, `UsingLength`, or `IsLineDep` do not update their existing policy;
   - Preview continues using stale policy values.

   Minimal fix: add one transactional policy upsert stored procedure and call it from the asset save transaction. For eligible fixed assets, create/update method 1, depreciation start date and useful-life months before any posted period exists; reject financial policy changes once a posted period exists.

2. Important — Financial-field locking fails open when the database check fails  
   Files:
   - `1.WIN-FORM/FamObject/FAM_DeviceDepPolicy.cs:11-16`
   - `1.WIN-FORM/FamManager/Device/frmDeviceDetail.cs:325-326`
   - `1.WIN-FORM/FamManager/Device/frmDeviceDetail.cs:530-578`

   `HasPostedPeriod()` returns `false` when the stored procedure fails and `GetDataTable()` returns `null`. The form interprets that as “no posted depreciation,” unlocks financial controls, and allows `FAM_Device.Update()` to overwrite values. This can occur during partial SQL deployment, connectivity errors, or a missing procedure.

   Minimal fix: distinguish “query failed” from a real `false`. Throw/return a failure state when the result is null or malformed, and abort loading/saving financial fields. The save path should fail closed unless the posted-period check completes successfully.

3. Important — The required migration does not deploy data in its checked-in default state  
   File: `2.SQL/patches/2026-10-19/FAM-DeviceDep/02_20261019_FAM_DeviceDepPolicy_migrate.sql:16-19, 213-224`

   `@IsCommit` is hard-coded to `0`, so running patches 01–19 in order leaves all legacy assets without policies and rolls back `IsLineDep = 1`. The application then has no assets to Preview/Post unless an operator manually edits the script before execution. This is a deployment-order/contract failure for the required default migration.

   Minimal fix: split preview and commit into separate numbered patches, or make the deployed migration commit by default after its validation guards. Keep a separate explicitly named read-only preview script if operational review is required.

4. Important — Office/place history is not immutable and can misstate posted ledger context  
   Files:
   - `2.SQL/patches/2026-10-19/FAM-DeviceDep/01_20261019_FAM_DeviceDep_schema.sql:193-219`
   - `2.SQL/patches/2026-10-19/FAM-DeviceDep/18_20261019_FAM_DeviceDepPeriodDetail_Search_display_names.sql:55-59, 83-89`
   - `2.SQL/patches/2026-10-19/FAM-DeviceDep/19_20261019_FAM_DeviceDepPeriodDetail_History_display_names.sql:53-57, 90-96`

   Detail rows snapshot code, name and status, but not `OfficeID` or `PlaceID`. Patches 18/19 display office/place by joining the current `FAM_Device` row. Moving an asset later rewrites the apparent office/place of an already posted period; history can even combine the period’s old office with the asset’s current place.

   Minimal fix: add office/place IDs and display names as detail snapshots, populate them during Post, and make detail/history procedures read those snapshot columns. Avoid joining mutable master assignment data for posted ledger history.

Other reviewed requirements—Preview being read-only, transactional Post/Reverse, per-asset later-period reversal guard, inventory save not updating depreciation values, .NET 4 syntax, and base classes not exposing entity CRUD—did not yield an additional concrete Critical/Important finding.
